title: Deployment Aftershock Playbook and Safety Cartography
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a staged canary promotion on 2026-02-25 we observed a rapid increase in corrupted outputs and tail latency for requests routed to the canary variant. Automated circuit-breakers did not trigger a timely rollback because the promotion signal relied on a single aggregated error-rate measurement with long hysteresis. Post-incident analysis indicates a confluence of factors: a KV-cache keyspace collision between two model variants (causing stale/incorrect KV loads), shadow-to-canary telemetry drift (shadow traffic did not exercise the same long-tail token distributions), and a routing fallback mismatch that allowed degraded canary instances to receive traffic under elevated load. Objective: produce an actionable aftershock playbook (safety runbook updates, telemetry contract, and automated verification artifacts) plus a "safety cartography" that maps failure surfaces to concrete detection points and mitigation levers. This ticket captures follow-ups, owners, and concrete experiments needed to harden future canary promotions.
actions: (A1) Add KV cache keyspace collision detector: instrument per-variant key prefix usage + alert if >0.1% key aliasing across variants. Owner: Liam Chen. Due: 2026-03-10.

(A2) Promote shadow parity gate: require histogram parity for token-length and latency P95 between shadow and canary for two synthetic prompt cohorts (short, long). Owner: PM (Ravi Kapoor) + Eng (Liam). Due: 2026-03-17.

(A3) Shorten rollback hysteresis and add multi-signal policy: require OR of (error-rate spike >3x baseline AND latency P99 delta >100ms) OR (synthetic-lab failures). Owner: Reliability squad. Due: 2026-03-12.

(A4) Implement rollback-proof artifact bundle for each promotion: include reproducible synthetic prompts, model config snapshot, kv-keyspace snapshot, and minimal failing trace. Owner: SRE + Eng. Due: 2026-03-20.
(A5) Run safety-lab chaos: inject synthetic KV collisions and 2x token-length tails in shadow traffic for three promotions to validate detection. Owner: Experiments team. Due: 2026-03-24.
(A6) Dashboard and runbook update PR: consolidate detection thresholds, play-by-play actions, and post-rollback checklist. Owner: Oncall runbook maintainer (Sofia Martinez). Due: 2026-03-14.
runbook_changes: Pre-promotion parity checklist: run synthetic parity suites and KV-keyspace validation before moving from shadow -> canary.
Promotion abort conditions: explicit thresholds for latency P99, model-level output-checker failures, and kv-collision alerts with 1-minute burst window.
Rollback steps: immediate traffic split to previous stable variant, preserve KV-keyspace snapshot, mark canary instances as quarantined, collect rollback-proof artifacts.
Post-rollback triage: automated ticket template, required logs/PRs linked, and a 72-hour monitoring hold with elevated telemetry sampling.
Safety-lab required sign-off: canary promotions of new model families must pass two safety-lab runs with zero critical failures before 10% traffic ramp.
telemetry_updates: Add per-variant KV-keyspace cardinality metric (kv.keyspace.cardinality.variant) and a collision-rate gauge.
Emit synthetic cohort parity results as time-series (parity.short_cohort, parity.long_cohort) with pass/fail boolean.
Instrument end-to-end trace annotations for shadow vs live routing decisions to correlate sample mismatches.
Expose rollback-proof artifact link in telemetry event when automated rollback occurs (trace id -> artifact bundle).
experiments: Synthetic KV collision injection: bench repeated key aliasing scenarios to measure degradation threshold and detection lead time.
Shadow traffic tail amplification: use generated long-token prompts to validate parity gating under heavy-tail inputs.
Hysteresis sweep: run controlled promotions while varying rollback hysteresis windows (30s, 60s, 3m) to find sweet-spot minimizing false positives and false negatives.
Automated rollback dry-run: simulate 'would-have-rolled-back' decisions in the next three promotions and log decision confidence scores.
links: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/402 (telemetry metrics for parity and collisions)
